background: Societe Generale is one of France's three largest banks, a universal bank with French retail networks, a large derivatives-driven investment bank, the Ayvens car-leasing business and banking subsidiaries in Africa and Central Europe.
synthesis: Rated A+ on average across all three and the weakest of them at A, but the outlooks disagree - one negative, one positive and one stable - after a two-notch upgrade by one of the three on 12 May 2026. Every ratio sits on the weak side of EU and Nordic banks: CET1 of 13.2% and leverage of 4.3% are both in the bottom quarter, LCR of 146% is below the median and NSFR of 115% is again in the bottom quarter. None has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026), so this is a settled position rather than a slide, but it leaves little headroom on any measure. The news has been constructive, with a raised profitability target on 22 Sep 2026 and one of the three moving to a positive outlook in June.
